newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada poised for strong growth, bank says.
newsitem.headline: Canada poised for strong growth, bank says.

text.p: The Canadian economy is poised for strong growth and a healthy rebound on the job front this year, said one of Canada's largest banks on Friday.

Canada's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow at 3.4 percent in 1997 and 3.8 percent, and 300,000 new jobs will be created in both 1997 and 1998, the Bank of Montreal said in its national economic outlook.
The bank is predicting a drop in the unemployment rate from 9.7 percent to 8.6 percent by the end of 1998.
Low interest rates, tame inflation and a surge in consumer spending will fuel growth, the bank said.
Consumer spending rose at an annual rate of 5.6 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, led by higher sales of big-ticket items such as homes, furniture and automobiles.
Housing starts and retail sales also continued to show strength, the bank said.
"There is evidence that the expansion has continued in the early part of this year," said Tim O'Neill, the bank's chief economist.
O'Neill said that Canada's exports will continue to benefit from a weak Canadian dollar, subdued domestic labor costs and relatively strong economic growth in the U.S.
Inflation will remain tame despite strong economic growth, the bank predicted.
The February consumer price index rose 2.2 percent from a year ago while the core rate of inflation, excluding the volatile food and energy components, is up only 1.5 percent.
"Even though we expect the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on March 25, the Bank of Canada will likely resist increasing interest rates," O'Neill said.
